**Values** describe qualities you want to bring to your actions. Curiosity, care, fairness, or reliability can guide many choices. A goal is an outcome or task you can complete; a value can keep guiding you after that goal is finished.

## Choose a direction that belongs to you

Consider an area of life you want to engage with more fully. What quality would you like to express there? Notice the difference between a direction you choose and a demand you feel you must satisfy to earn approval.

For example, being caring does not require always saying yes. A caring action can include a clear limit that protects your capacity to stay involved.

Use [Values & Valued Action](/tool-finder/values/) to explore directions that matter to you.

## Make the next step concrete

**Committed action** means putting a value into practice and learning from what happens. Choose a step small enough to fit your current circumstances. Name when and where you can take it, and consider an easier version for a difficult day.

A person who values connection might send one thoughtful message. Someone who values learning might spend ten minutes exploring a question. Neither action needs to solve an entire area of life.

## Include obstacles in the plan

Some obstacles are practical: limited time, money, health, access, or safety. Address these rather than interpreting every barrier as unwillingness. Other obstacles are inner experiences, such as embarrassment or a familiar prediction of failure. Acceptance and defusion may help you take a workable step alongside them.

If a plan repeatedly fails, change the plan. Commitment to a value does not require rigid commitment to one method.

## Try it: a small commitment

Make a short note covering your chosen direction, the next action, and a likely obstacle. Add a fallback action that still expresses the value. Afterward, review what happened and what you want to adjust.

Use the [SMART Goal Builder](/tool-finder/goal-builder/) to specify the action and [Values Review](/tool-finder/values-review/) to revisit it. These tools support saving and reopening your notes.

## Review the action, not just the feeling

A useful review asks what you did, what you learned, and whether the action expressed your chosen direction. Feeling nervous afterward does not by itself mean the action was wrong. Equally, commitment does not mean repeating a plan that is unsafe or unsuitable.

The [Values Review tool](/tool-finder/values-review/) now includes a reflection on thoughts that pulled you off course and what helped you respond flexibly. Use [Unhooking from Thoughts](/tool-finder/act-unhooking/) or [Making Room for Feelings](/tool-finder/act-making-room/) when an inner obstacle needs attention.

For a busy week, caring might mean arranging a short call rather than a long visit. The action changes with your circumstances; the quality you want to express can remain.
